general.title: Getting Started
general.summary: Learn the NEXORIA dashboard, server management, modules, commands, variables, and account features.

sections.heading: Using the website
sections.body: Sign in with Discord, choose a server, and use the server tabs to manage NEXORIA features. Documentation and policy pages can be opened directly from the website.

sections.heading: Offline-safe documentation
sections.body: The documentation bundle is designed to remain readable when live service features are temporarily unavailable.

sections.heading: Security note
sections.body: Internal service addresses, deployment commands, service connection ports, deployment link details, credentials, and local filesystem paths are intentionally not published in public documentation.

sections.heading: Discord OAuth2 setup
sections.body: Website sign-in: identify and guilds. Bot installation: bot and applications.commands. Those four are the scopes NEXORIA currently needs. The bot permission bitfield is 268528848, covering View Channel, Send Messages, Embed Links, Read Message History, Add Reactions, Manage Messages, Manage Roles, Manage Channels, and View Audit Log. The current app does not need email, connections, guilds.join, guilds.members.read, gdm.join, rpc, RPC notifications/voice/video/screenshare/activities, webhook.incoming, messages.read, applications.builds.read, applications.store.update, applications.entitlements, openid, or applications.commands.permissions.update. Requesting those later should be tied to a specific feature and its documented need rather than enabled preemptively.

general.title: Module System
general.summary: NEXORIA modules can provide dashboard UI, server-side routes, documentation, commands, and leaderboard data.

sections.heading: Module layout
sections.body: Each module lives under Modules/<module>/ with Code and Documentation folders. Server code is loaded from Code/<module>_server.js.

sections.heading: Retries and isolation
sections.body: Dashboard module assets are loaded independently. A failed module is skipped and retried so one module should not prevent the rest of the dashboard from rendering.

sections.heading: Extensibility
sections.body: The server exposes provider hooks so modules can contribute custom-command entries and leaderboard data without owning the shared dashboard route.

general.title: Configuration
general.summary: Public website configuration, privacy boundaries, and safe configuration practices.

sections.heading: Public JSON
sections.body: The public site configuration contains only values required for normal website operation. Sensitive credentials and private service details are kept out of the public bundle.

sections.heading: Secrets
sections.body: config.env contains private bot and admin credentials. It is not part of the public site bundle.

sections.heading: Backups
sections.body: Important JSON writes use temporary files and local backups under Data/Backups so a failed write does not immediately destroy the previous copy.

general.title: Status and Refreshing
general.summary: The dashboard continuously checks the service connection and can recover after the bot comes back online.

sections.heading: Checking state
sections.body: The dashboard shows a neutral checking state while service status is being refreshed. If the service cannot be reached, the UI reports that state and continues background checks.

sections.heading: Refresh intervals
sections.body: Refresh behavior is designed to avoid unnecessary requests and to recover gracefully after temporary failures.

general.title: Terminal Announcements
general.summary: The bot terminal can open a paste-friendly announcement prompt and send the finished text to a configured Discord channel or the owner.

sections.heading: Using announce
sections.body: Type announce in the bot terminal, paste or type the announcement, then enter SEND on its own line. Enter CANCEL to discard it. Blank lines are preserved.

sections.heading: Destination
sections.body: The destination is configured with ANNOUNCEMENT_CHANNEL_ID, ANNOUNCEMENT_OWNER_ID, and ANNOUNCEMENT_TARGET in config.env. The feature can be disabled with ANNOUNCEMENTS_ENABLED or the announcement channel server’s General Settings toggle.

general.title: Website & Navigation
general.summary: How the public NEXORIA website is organized and where to find its main features.

sections.heading: Main Menu
sections.body: The Main Menu is the public landing area. It provides the bot invite, Dashboard, Support Server, and Leaderboards links. The Support Server opens Discord in a new tab.

sections.heading: Documentation
sections.body: Documentation is available from the site even when the service is offline. It is grouped into website topics, configuration, status/refreshing, announcements, and module documentation. Use the search box to find a topic.

sections.heading: Support Server
sections.body: The NEXORIA Support Server is the place to ask for help, report issues, and suggest new languages or features. The support button opens the configured Discord server in a new browser tab.

sections.heading: Dashboard
sections.body: After signing in with Discord, Dashboard lets you select a server and access the modules enabled for that server. Server owners control dashboard access in General Settings.

sections.heading: Leaderboards
sections.body: Leaderboards is a public page for leaderboard providers supplied by NEXORIA modules. Modules can register their own leaderboard data through the shared provider system.

general.title: General Settings
general.summary: Server-owner controls that affect dashboard access, audit logs, leaderboards, and terminal announcements.

sections.heading: Dashboard access
sections.body: Server owners can choose whether dashboard access is available to everyone, administrators, or selected roles. The owner always retains access.

sections.heading: Audit Log access
sections.body: Audit Log access can be restricted to the owner, everyone, administrators, or selected roles. This controls who can view the server's NEXORIA audit entries.

sections.heading: Leaderboard visibility
sections.body: The leaderboard setting controls whether leaderboard data is available for the server. Module providers can still define the actual data and presentation.

sections.heading: Terminal announcements
sections.body: The server owner can disable terminal announcements from General Settings. The terminal feature can also be disabled globally with ANNOUNCEMENTS_ENABLED in config.env.

sections.heading: Refresh settings
sections.body: The website stores refresh preferences locally in the browser. Status and leaderboard polling can be changed without modifying the bot's core code.

general.title: NEXORIA AI
general.summary: The built-in documentation assistant answers from the documentation bundle without an external AI API.

sections.heading: What it can answer
sections.body: The assistant searches published NEXORIA documentation. It can explain documented features, tell you where a setting or page is located, and provide direct links when the documentation includes a matching destination.

sections.heading: No API key
sections.body: The assistant is a standalone client-side documentation search system. It does not require an OpenAI key or another external AI service.

sections.heading: Conversation storage
sections.body: When the bot is online and a Discord login is available, conversation data is stored encrypted on the local bot PC using the Discord user ID as the local record identifier. When the bot is offline, the browser stores an encrypted copy in IndexedDB using a browser-local non-extractable key. The website does not put conversation plaintext into a public JSON file.

general.title: Complete Feature Reference
general.summary: A practical overview of the dashboard, authentication, documentation AI, leaderboards, server management and offline-safe behavior.

sections.heading: Discord authentication
sections.body: NEXORIA uses Discord OAuth to identify the signed-in user and load the servers they can manage. A valid saved session is reused automatically. Logging out removes the saved session so the dashboard will not silently reuse that account until the user signs in again.

sections.heading: Offline-safe behavior
sections.body: The website continues to show cached documentation and can queue AI errors and conversation data locally when the bot service connection is unavailable. When the bot becomes reachable again, queued data is synchronized to the bot PC where appropriate.

sections.heading: Documentation search
sections.body: Documentation can be searched by module, feature, setting, command, variable or descriptive text. Selecting a result updates the article without leaving the documentation view. The Ask NEXORIA AI button opens the documentation assistant in the same interface.

sections.heading: Leaderboard controls
sections.body: Leaderboards support module-specific results, configurable result limits, pagination, refresh, and cached data when the bot is temporarily unavailable. Server entries can show rating and vote information when supplied by the module.

sections.heading: Server and profile imagery
sections.body: Discord server and user images are displayed with fixed square containers and object-fit cropping so different avatar dimensions do not stretch the dashboard layout.

modules.title: Custom Commands
modules.summary: Build prefix and slash commands with a visual node graph, branching conditions, roles, persistent Advanced variables, a simulator, and execution controls.

sections.heading: Basic mode — quick commands
sections.body: Basic mode is for a straightforward trigger → response command. Choose Prefix or Slash, enter the trigger, add the response, choose who can run it, then save. Use Basic when the command only needs a small number of ordered actions and no visual branching.

sections.heading: Advanced mode — visual command flows
sections.body: Advanced mode opens an empty canvas for a new command. Add exactly one Trigger node, then connect its output to the first executable node. Nothing is inserted automatically. Existing commands are migrated into their graph without changing their saved behavior.

sections.heading: Every Advanced node
sections.body: Trigger — required entry node; exactly one is allowed per command. Description — slash-command metadata. Permissions — execution access. Send Message — sends text and supports built-in and Advanced variables. Send Embed — title, description, color and variables. Reply — replies to the trigger. Mention User — mentions the command user. Add Role / Remove Role — role changes. React — adds a reaction. DM User — sends a DM. Delete Trigger — deletes the prefix trigger message. Wait — delays execution. Stop — ends the flow. If — searchable Target → Condition → Value/Role logic. If Contains — text branch. If Has Role — role branch. Random Chance — percentage branch. Comment — builder note. Set Variable — writes a persistent Advanced variable when one exists, otherwise a flow-local value. Change Variable — adds/subtracts a number. Log — diagnostic output. If Number — numeric comparisons with True/False outputs. If Variable Exists — checks whether an Advanced variable can be read. Random Pick — stores a random comma-separated option in a variable. Set Channel Topic — updates the current text-channel topic. Pin Trigger / Unpin Trigger — manage the triggering message pin. Clear Reactions — removes reactions from the triggering message.

sections.heading: Command nodes
sections.body: Trigger is required and defines the command name, trigger text, prefix/slash mode, scope, and slash description. Description stores a slash-command description when you want metadata separate from Trigger. Permissions controls Everyone, Administrators, or selected roles. These metadata nodes configure the command and are not sent to Discord as actions.

sections.heading: Discord action nodes
sections.body: Send Message sends normal text and supports documented variables. Send Embed creates a title, description, and color. Reply replies to the triggering message. Mention User adds the command user's mention. Add Role and Remove Role change a member's roles when the bot can manage the target role. React reacts to the triggering message. DM User sends a direct message. Delete Trigger removes the triggering prefix message when Discord permissions allow it.

sections.heading: Flow nodes
sections.body: Wait pauses execution for a controlled number of milliseconds. Stop ends execution immediately. Connect output ports directly to input ports; a normal input accepts one incoming connection. Wires move with nodes and can be selected and removed from the custom editor menu.

sections.heading: Logic and condition nodes
sections.body: If is the flexible condition node. Choose a Target such as User, Message, Channel, Command, or Variable, then choose the matching condition and value/role. User supports Has Role, Doesn't Have Role, Is Administrator, and Is Server Owner. Message supports Contains, Doesn't Contain, Equals, and Doesn't Equal. Channel can check text, thread, and forum types. Command can compare name or trigger. Variable compares a stored command variable. Random Chance branches by percentage. Branch nodes expose separate True and False outputs.

sections.heading: Variable nodes and custom variables
sections.body: Advanced variables are persistent and are available across Advanced custom commands in the same server. Create, rename, edit, search, delete, and insert them into message fields. Set Variable and Change Variable can update persistent Advanced variables. Basic mode remains isolated and does not expose this persistent variable system. Use {var.name} for command-local legacy values and {name} for an Advanced variable.

sections.heading: Utility nodes
sections.body: Log writes a diagnostic line to the bot console and is useful while debugging a flow. Comment is a builder-only note and never sends a Discord message. Use comments to explain why a branch or variable exists.

sections.heading: Preview, validation, and console
sections.body: Run opens the custom preview. It simulates a user invoking the command, shows bot replies as a conversation, evaluates branches, and records diagnostics. Preview runs do not change Discord. Nodes with missing required data receive a red problem outline. The console stays available between preview runs until Clear console is pressed.

sections.heading: Editing and navigation
sections.body: Drag a node header to move it. Drag directly from an output port to an input port to create a wire. Right-click inside the builder opens only the NEXORIA editor menu with relevant actions such as Duplicate, Center, Delete, Remove connection, and Add node here. Back and Exit both respect unsaved changes and ask before leaving. Use Cancel/Back to leave the editor without accidentally navigating outside the command workflow.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.body: Role gate: Trigger /staff → If (User → Has Role → Staff) → True → Add Role/Send Message; False → Send Message. Variable counter: Trigger ?count → Set Variable count=1 → Change Variable count +1 → Send Message "Count: {count}". Conditional text: Trigger ?hello → If (Message → Contains → hello) → True → Reply "Hello!"; False → Reply "Try saying hello.".

sections.heading: Built-in commands
sections.body: NEXORIA ships built-in commands such as /dashboard, /help, and /status. Built-ins stay in the command list for permission/category management and can be disabled or re-enabled by the server owner, but they cannot be deleted.

sections.heading: Shared variables across servers
sections.body: Advanced variables are private by default. An owner can enable read access, write access, or both. Enabling sharing generates a long-lived token. The token is stored as a hash and is shown when it is generated. A connected variable only permits operations allowed by the source variable. If a flow tries to read a write-only variable, or write to a read-only variable, the node is marked with a red problem outline and the run is blocked for that operation. Revoke sharing by turning both permissions off and generate a new token if needed.

sections.heading: Advanced variable manager
sections.body: The Custom Commands page contains an Advanced variables manager with search, value editing, deletion, sharing, and token connection. Clicking a variable takes you to its first known node location when the variable is used in a command.

sections.heading: Examples with variables
sections.body: Trigger /welcome → Send Message "Welcome {user.mention} to {server.name}. Trigger: {command.trigger}". Persistent counter: Trigger /count → Set Variable visits=1 → Change Variable visits +1 → Send Message "Visits: {visits}". Shared read-only value: Trigger /info → If Target=Variable, choose visits, Condition=Contains, Value=1 → True → Send Message "Matched {visits}".

modules.title: Logging
modules.summary: Server activity logging — pick a channel per log type (or per whole category), self-posted or via webhook, with ignore lists for noisy channels/roles/users.

sections.heading: Log types
sections.body: Grouped into categories (Bot, Custom Commands, Applications, Channels, Roles, Members, Messages, Voice, and more) — expand a category to set a channel for each type inside it individually, or set the whole category at once. Custom Command Used records custom command execution with the user, channel, and command name.

sections.heading: Self-post vs. webhook
sections.body: By default NEXORIA posts log messages itself. A channel can instead be set to use a webhook — useful for custom branding in that channel — but since anyone who obtains the webhook URL can post to it, this is opt-in per channel with a warning before you turn it on.

sections.heading: Ignore lists
sections.body: Channels, roles, and users can be excluded from logging entirely, so noisy bots or a specific channel don't flood your log channels.

sections.heading: Category layout
sections.body: Logging is organized as a hierarchy: category → individual event types → destination settings. The indentation and category controls make it clear which event belongs to which group, while disabled destinations remain visibly muted.

modules.title: Ticket Tool
modules.summary: Support tickets: panels users click to open a ticket, per-subject settings, staff claiming, closing DMs, share links, and insights.

sections.heading: Panels
sections.body: A panel is a message (plain text and/or an embed) with buttons or a dropdown that users click to open a ticket. Each option on a panel connects to a Ticket Template (a "subject"), so one panel can offer several kinds of tickets at once.

sections.heading: Subjects (Ticket Templates)
sections.body: Each subject has its own welcome message, close message, staff roles, user/staff/claimer channel permissions, ticket limits, creation cooldowns, an optional auto-close timer, and its own logging toggles.

sections.heading: Claiming & Staff-Only Claim
sections.body: Staff can claim a ticket to signal they're handling it. When Staff-Only Claim is on, only members with a staff role for that subject can claim.

sections.heading: Closing DM
sections.body: A guild-wide, customizable embed DM sent to whoever opened a ticket once it's closed, separate from a subject's own plain-text close message. Supports {ticket.url} — a link back to the person's own authenticated ticket page.

sections.heading: Share Links
sections.body: When sharing is turned on, a closed ticket can be given a public, read-only share link so its transcript can be sent to someone without dashboard access.

sections.heading: Insights
sections.body: Ticket volume, close rate, and staff performance over a selectable time period, computed from real ticket data — nothing here is simulated.

sections.heading: Ticket workflow
sections.body: Ticket configuration covers creation, opener messages, transcript handling, claim/close behavior, support roles and channel destinations. Use the module's settings panels to review each option; values are stored per server.
